Goal: Demo Video

Generate a 30-second demo video for this project as one self-contained HTML/JavaScript animation that presents its main goals and key features, grounded only in what you read in the repository, with a matching on-device narration track per the audio policy in the persona. Save it with a single project_demo_video_write call.

The demo video is saved to `session-manager-operations/project-pages/demo-video/index.html`. It's 9.9 KB, 30 seconds, and has no narration.

**No audio and no visual check:**
- **Narration:** I generated a Kokoro (`af_heart`) track that fit the six scenes, but I left it out. The tool only accepts the document as inline text, so I would have had to retype about 320 KB of base64 audio by hand. The audio policy allows a silent video as the fallback. The captions on screen carry the same lines. The track is in `/tmp/demo-build/n.mp3` if you want it embedded another way.
- **Playback:** I couldn't test it in a browser because Playwright's Chromium isn't installed here. I only syntax-checked the script with Node.

**Storyboard and sources:**

| Scene | Time | Claim | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Title | 0–5s | bilko.run, "host platform for Bilko's independent AI tools" | `package.json` description |
| Platform | 5–9s | Host platform, not a product. Every tool is an independent app (Outdoor-Hours, Local-Score, Bilko-Academy, Stepproof as spokes) | `CLAUDE.md` |
| Shared services | 9–14s | Clerk auth, Stripe credits, component kit, brand chrome | `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/host-contract.md` |
| Static-path contract | 14–20s | An app built in a sibling repo is served at `/projects/<slug>/` | `docs/host-contract.md` |
| Tooling | 20–25s | `bilko-host` MCP (register, publish, inspect) and `host-kit` (`authFetch`, `useAuth`, `SiteHeader`) | `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/host-contract.md` |
| Closing | 25–30s | `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev`; React, Fastify, Clerk, Stripe, Gemini | `README.md` |

The video uses a single `requestAnimationFrame` clock and exposes `window.smDemo`. It has play/pause, restart, a progress bar, light and dark palettes, and a step-through mode for `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.
- When showing a time, include the zone abbreviation (e.g., "3:15 PM PDT") so it is unambiguous.
- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.
- Don't offer a fast-but-partial path as an option; pick the thorough, correct solution by default.
- When the choice is "do A, do B, or do both", always do both A and B — do not ask which.
- Treat inclusive options as a signal to deliver the complete set, not to pick one.

## Automation model pinning

Any script or process that shells out to `claude --print` / `claude -p` **must** pin `--model`
explicitly.

Unpinned calls inherit whatever the CLI's current default model is, which drifts over time
(e.g. Opus → Fable) — silently and unboundedly multiplying the cost of batch/cron automation
that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

When writing *or reviewing* any `claude -p` call site — PRD executors, bots, classifiers, hooks
— check for an explicit `--model` flag before shipping it.

## Default to acting; never ask permission to improve

Filing feedback, queuing a PRD, routing a finding, or running an improvement step is the
**default action, not a question**. Never end a turn with "want me to file this?", "should I
queue this?", or "should I send feedback to X?". Do it, then report what was filed or queued.

Route findings immediately by ownership, without a confirmation prompt:

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| This project | `/develop` |
| Another service | `/my-feedback` to that project |
| Nothing actionable | Say so explicitly |

The only questions worth asking are genuine scope or decision ambiguities that would cost real
rework — never permission to perform the standard improvement action.

## What This Is

bilko.run is Bilko's personal brand site and host platform. Each app is its own product with its own page, scoring engine, and UX — they are NOT features of one product.

Three host kinds, declared in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts`. Full spec in [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

| Kind | Path | When to use |
|---|---|---|

- `/projects/<slug>/` (trailing slash, static-path) → served by Fastify static, never hits the SPA

## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.
- When showing a time, include the zone abbreviation (e.g., "3:15 PM PDT") so it is unambiguous.
- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.
- Don't offer a fast-but-partial path as an option; pick the thorough, correct solution by default.
- When the choice is "do A, do B, or do both", always do both A and B — do not ask which.
- Treat inclusive options as a signal to deliver the complete set, not to pick one.

## Automation model pinning

Any script or process that shells out to `claude --print` / `claude -p` **must** pin `--model`
explicitly.

Unpinned calls inherit whatever the CLI's current default model is, which drifts over time
(e.g. Opus → Fable) — silently and unboundedly multiplying the cost of batch/cron automation
that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

When writing *or reviewing* any `claude -p` call site — PRD executors, bots, classifiers, hooks
— check for an explicit `--model` flag before shipping it.

## Default to acting; never ask permission to improve

Filing feedback, queuing a PRD, routing a finding, or running an improvement step is the
**default action, not a question**. Never end a turn with "want me to file this?", "should I
queue this?", or "should I send feedback to X?". Do it, then report what was filed or queued.

Route findings immediately by ownership, without a confirmation prompt:

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| This project | `/develop` |
| Another service | `/my-feedback` to that project |
| Nothing actionable | Say so explicitly |

The only questions worth asking are genuine scope or decision ambiguities that would cost real
rework — never permission to perform the standard improvement action.

### Shared Component Kit (`src/components/tool-page/`)

### host-kit (`packages/host-kit/`)
This is the client SDK that static-path siblings use. It provides `authFetch`/`useAuth` (Clerk Bearer auth to the host's `/api`), the games hooks, `SiteHeader`, `GameShell`, and the `bilko-host-kit` manifest CLI. It is a pnpm workspace package with its own build and tests (`pnpm --filter host-kit build|test|typecheck`).

All 14 sibling consumers depend on it locally with `"host-kit": "file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit"`. None of them use npm. Those consumers are the 8 AI-tool pages, Stepproof, Academy, Sudoku, Etch, Fizzpop and MindSwiffer.
- **After changing it:** pnpm copies the untracked `dist/` into each app. Run `pnpm --filter host-kit build` here, then `pnpm install` in each app.
- **Tailwind:** apps that render its components need `@source "<rel>/node_modules/host-kit/dist";` in their Tailwind CSS, because Tailwind skips `node_modules`.
- **Changesets:** add a `.changeset/*.md` (root `.changeset/`) for each change.
- **npm releases:** optional. Push a `host-kit-vX.Y.Z` tag to run `.github/workflows/host-kit-release.yml`. This needs an `NPM_AUTOMATION_TOKEN` repo secret.
- **History:** merged in from `StanislavBG/bilko-host-kit` (now archived) on 2026-10-04, with its full history.

### Shared Hooks (`src/hooks/`)
- `useAuth` — Clerk auth state
- `usePageView` — Page view tracking with Clerk email

### Backend Patterns (`server/`)
- `server/routes/tools/` — One file per AI tool. `_shared.ts` holds the rate limiter, IP hashing, usage tracking, and the inverse-mode generator helper. `index.ts` is the barrel that registers all tools. To extract a tool to a sibling repo, lift its file + the page; no other server changes required.
- `server/routes/blog.ts` — Blog CRUD (admin-only writes)
- `server/routes/stripe.ts` — Checkout, webhooks, billing portal
- `server/routes/analytics.ts` — Page views + admin stats dashboard (`/api/analytics/event` is open to same-origin sibling apps for `track()`)

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for

# Bilko host contract

bilko.run is a **host platform**, not a single product. It hosts many independent "apps" — each with its own product, its own scoring engine, its own UX. Some apps live in this repo; some live in their own repos and are dropped in as static assets; some live on other domains.

This document defines the contract: what the host provides, what an app must implement, and how to add a new app. Host-internal implementation detail (monitoring, QA gates, cost controls, caching, observability, security headers) lives in [`docs/host-internals.md`](host-internals.md) — read that only if you're changing the host itself, not when you're publishing an app.

## The three host kinds

Every app declares one host kind in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts` (react-route) or `src/data/standalone-projects.json` (static-path / external-url):

| Kind | When to use | Path | Coupling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | App needs the shared auth/credit/component kit and is small enough to live alongside the others | `/products/<slug>` | Tight — same Vite build, same Fastify server |
| `static-path` | App is built in its own repo (often its own Claude session) and just needs a URL on bilko.run | `/projects/<slug>/` | Loose — host serves prebuilt static assets, no shared runtime |
| `external-url` | App lives on another domain or subdomain | `https://<host>/...` | None — host only links to it |

Default to `static-path` for new apps — including ones that need a signed-in user (see "Calling authenticated host APIs from a `static-path` app" below). `react-route` is for the AI-tool family that already shares the kit.

## What the host provides

These are the OS services. Apps use them; they should not reimplement.

### To every app, regardless of host kind

- **Brand chrome.** Header, footer, blog, /pricing, /privacy, /terms, /admin, ⌘K command palette.
- **Portfolio listing.** Anything in the registry shows up on `/`, `/products`, and ⌘K automatically. No manual wiring.
- **Domain.** `bilko.run/<your-path>`.

### To `react-route` apps additionally

- **Auth: Clerk.** Available via `useUser()` and `useAuth()` from `@clerk/clerk-react`. Server-side: `requireAuth(req, reply)` from `server/clerk.ts` returns the Clerk email or 401s.
- **Credits: token wallet.** Spend via `deductToken(email)` and check via `getTokenBalance(email)` from `server/services/tokens.ts`. Free users get a starter grant via `grantFreeTokens(email)`.
- **Payments: Stripe.** Subscription state via `getActiveSubscriptionLive(email)`; one-time purchases via `hasPurchased(email, productKey)`. Both from `server/services/stripe.ts`.
- **Rate limiting.** `checkRateLimit(ipHash, endpoint, email?, productKey?)` from `server/routes/tools/_shared.ts` — handles free-tier daily caps, paid-tier caps, pro-skip.
- **Page-view analytics.** `usePageView()` hook fires once per route mount.
- **Component kit.** `src/components/tool-page/` — `ToolHero`, `ScoreCard`, `SectionBreakdown`, `CompareLayout`, `Rewrites`, `CrossPromo`, `colors.ts`. Use these instead of building custom UI for grade/score displays.
- **Tool API hook.** `useToolApi()` in `src/hooks/` wraps auth, submit, compare, generate, error/loading/token state.
- **Gemini.** `askGemini(prompt, opts)` from `server/gemini.ts`. Use `parseJsonResponse` (re-exported as `parseResult` in `_shared.ts`) for JSON outputs.
- **Database.** Turso/libSQL via `dbGet/dbAll/dbRun/dbTransaction` from `server/db.ts`. Falls back to local SQLite in dev. All SQL parameterized.

### To `static-path` and `external-url` apps additionally

- **No shared runtime.** Bring your own runtime and your own UI. The host serves the bytes. It does not inject the Clerk SDK, the component kit, or any providers into your page.

### Calling authenticated host APIs from a `static-path` app

A `static-path` app is same-origin with `/api`, so it *can* call authenticated host endpoints (`/api/games/*`, the AI-tool gateways, `/api/academy/*`). There is **one supported way to authenticate: send a Clerk session JWT in `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.** `requireAuth` / `requireAdmin` in `server/clerk.ts` read only that header.

- **Cookies are not accepted.** Clerk's first-party `__session` cookie on bilko.run is **not** read by the host, and `credentials: 'include'` by itself always gets a 401. This is deliberate. That cookie is a 60-second token that only clerk-js refreshes. A static page that doesn't run clerk-js would get intermittent 401s about a minute after page load. Accepting it would also make every mutating `/api` route cookie-authenticated, which means CSRF exposure.
- **How to get the token:** load clerk-js from the host's Clerk Frontend API (`https://clerk.bilko.run/npm/@clerk/clerk-js@5/dist/clerk.browser.js`, with the bilko.run publishable key as `data-clerk-publishable-key`). Call `await Clerk.load()`, then `await Clerk.session?.getToken()` before **each** request. Don't cache the token, because clerk-js already caches and refreshes it. The host CSP already allows `clerk.bilko.run` in `script-src`. Copy the CSP nonce from `<meta name="csp-nonce">` onto the script tag. **Use host-kit instead of rolling your own:** `authFetch(url, init)` (`getAuthToken()`, `useAuth()`, `openSignIn()`) from `host-kit` does all of this. The `useSaveState` / `useUnlocks` / `useLeaderboard` hooks already use it.
- **Gate the load cheaply:** a `__client_uat` cookie value > 0 means the user has signed in on bilko.run. If it is absent or `0`, treat the user as signed out without downloading clerk-js.
- **Identity on the server** is always the email from the verified token. Never trust a user id or email in the request body.

## What an app must implement

A registry entry — a `static-path`/`external-url` entry in `src/data/standalone-projects.json` (validated by `mcp-host-server/src/contract/registry.ts`; see "Registry rules" below), or a `react-route` entry in `src/config/tools.ts`. Sibling repos add theirs via the [`bilko-host` MCP](../mcp-host-server/README.md) — never by hand-editing this repo.

<style>
:root{--bg:#f6f5f1;--fg:#16181d;--mut:#555b66;--card:#fff;--line:#c9ccd3;--acc:#c2410c;--acc2:#0f766e}
@media(prefers-color-scheme:dark){:root{--bg:#0f1115;--fg:#f2f3f5;--mut:#a3a9b5;--card:#1a1d24;--line:#343945;--acc:#fb923c;--acc2:#2dd4bf}}
*{box-sizing:border-box}html,body{margin:0;height:100%;background:var(--bg);color:var(--fg);font-family:system-ui,-apple-system,"Segoe UI",Roboto,sans-serif;overflow:hidden}
#wrap{position:fixed;inset:0;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center}
#stage{width:1280px;height:720px;position:relative;transform-origin:center center;flex:none;overflow:hidden;background:var(--bg)}
.scene{position:absolute;inset:0 0 56px 0;display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;justify-content:center;opacity:0;padding:0 80px;text-align:center}
.a{opacity:0}
h1{font-size:120px;margin:0;letter-spacing:-3px}h1 b{color:var(--acc)}
h2{font-size:58px;margin:0 0 36px;line-height:1.15;letter-spacing:-1px;max-width:1080px}
.sub{font-size:36px;color:var(--mut);margin-top:22px;max-width:960px}
.row{display:flex;gap:26px;justify-content:center;align-items:stretch}
.card{background:var(--card);border:2px solid var(--line);border-radius:18px;padding:26px 28px;min-width:230px;font-size:30px;font-weight:600}
.card small{display:block;font-size:22px;color:var(--mut);font-weight:400;margin-top:8px}
.hub{background:var(--acc);color:#fff;border-radius:50%;width:150px;height:150px;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:34px;font-weight:700}
code,.mono{font-family:ui-monospace,Menlo,Consolas,monospace}
.term{background:#0b0d12;color:#e8eaf0;border-radius:16px;padding:30px 44px;font-size:46px;text-align:left;min-width:560px}
.term i{color:#2dd4bf;font-style:normal}
.cap{position:absolute;left:0;right:0;bottom:78px;text-align:center;font-size:28px;color:var(--mut)}
#bar{position:absolute;left:0;right:0;bottom:0;height:56px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:14px;padding:0 20px;background:var(--card);border-top:1px solid var(--line)}
#bar button{font:inherit;font-size:20px;background:none;color:var(--fg);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:8px;padding:4px 14px;cursor:pointer}
#prog{flex:1;height:8px;background:var(--line);border-radius:4px;cursor:pointer;position:relative}
#fill{position:absolute;left:0;top:0;bottom:0;width:0;background:var(--acc);border-radius:4px}
#time{font-size:18px;color:var(--mut);min-width:90px;text-align:right}
#snd{display:none}
.step{display:none}

<script>
const D=30;
const SC=[[0,5,"bilko.run — host platform for Bilko’s independent AI tools"],[5,9,"A host platform, not a product. Every tool is its own app."],[9,14,"Shared sign-in, credits, components, and brand chrome."],[14,20,"Apps live in their own repos, served at /projects/<slug>/."],[20,25,"Publish with the bilko-host MCP and host-kit."],[25,30,"pnpm install, then pnpm dev."]];
const $=(i)=>document.getElementById(i);
const stage=$("stage"),au=$("au"),scenes=SC.map((_,i)=>$("s"+i));
const reduced=matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;
const clamp=(x,a,b)=>Math.min(b,Math.max(a,x));
const type=(el,s,lt,d)=>{el.textContent=s.slice(0,Math.floor(clamp((lt-d)/0.06,0,s.length)))};
const render=(t)=>{
  t=clamp(t,0,D);
  SC.forEach(([a,b,c],i)=>{
    const el=scenes[i],lt=t-a,on=t>=a&&(t<b||(i===SC.length-1&&t>=b));
    const op=on?clamp(lt/0.4,0,1)*(i===SC.length-1?1:clamp((b-t)/0.4,0,1)):0;
    el.style.opacity=op;el.style.visibility=on?"visible":"hidden";
    el.querySelectorAll(".a").forEach((n)=>{
      const p=clamp((lt-parseFloat(n.dataset.d))/0.5,0,1);
      n.style.opacity=p;n.style.transform=n.tagName==="line"||n.tagName==="g"?"none":"translateY("+((1-p)*24)+"px)";
    });
    if(on&&i===3){const k=((lt-2)%1.6)/1.6,d=$("dot");d.setAttribute("cx",300+k*390);d.setAttribute("opacity",lt>2?1:0)}
    if(i===5){type($("t1"),"pnpm install",lt,1.0);type($("t2"),"pnpm dev",lt,2.2)}
    if(on)$("cap").textContent=c;
  });
  $("fill").style.width=(t/D*100)+"%";$("time").textContent=t.toFixed(1)+" / "+D;
};
let t=0,playing=false,last=0;
const sync=()=>{if(Math.abs(au.currentTime-t)>0.25)au.currentTime=t};
const tick=(now)=>{
  if(!playing)return;
  t=Math.min(D,t+(now-last)/1000);last=now;render(t);
  if(!reduced)sync();
  if(t>=D){pause();return}
  requestAnimationFrame(tick);
};
const play=()=>{
  if(reduced)return;
  if(t>=D)t=0;playing=true;last=performance.now();$("pp").textContent="❚❚";
  au.currentTime=t;const pr=au.play();
  if(pr&&pr.catch)pr.catch(()=>{$("snd").style.display="inline-block"});
  requestAnimationFrame(tick);
};
const pause=()=>{playing=false;au.pause();$("pp").textContent="▶"};
const seek=(x)=>{t=clamp(x,0,D);render(t);try{au.currentTime=t}catch(e){}};
window.smDemo={duration:D,seek,play,pause};
$("pp").onclick=()=>{playing?pause():play()};
$("rs").onclick=()=>{seek(0);reduced?0:play()};
$("snd").onclick=()=>{$("snd").style.display="none";au.currentTime=t;au.play()};
$("prog").onclick=(e)=>{const r=$("prog").getBoundingClientRect();seek((e.clientX-r.left)/r.width*D)};
const stepTo=(i)=>{i=clamp(i,0,SC.length-1);seek(SC[i][1]-0.05-(i===SC.length-1?0:0.4))};
const cur=()=>{const i=SC.findIndex(([a,b])=>t<b);return i<0?SC.length-1:i};
$("pv").onclick=()=>stepTo(cur()-1);$("nx").onclick=()=>stepTo(cur()+1);
const fit=()=>{const s=Math.min(innerWidth/1280,innerHeight/720);stage.style.transform="scale("+s+")"};
addEventListener("resize",fit);fit();
if(reduced){document.querySelectorAll(".step").forEach((n)=>n.style.display="inline-block");$("pp").style.display="none";stepTo(0)}
else{render(0);play()}
</script></body></html>
